leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eleven round-1 files name B037 as the preferred configuration. All five include Autor and Hanson and describe credible quasi-experimental evidence on import competition, plus a conceptual account of technology and labour demand. They differ on the third laureate. Enflo, Fredriksson and Hjalmarsson name Katz, and their citations cover the skill-premium and task framework as well as the trade-shock evidence. Dreber and Hassler name Dorn and tie the citation more closely to the import-shock papers; Hassler's citation is the narrowest, 'empirical analysis'. Dreber, Fredriksson, Enflo and Hjalmarsson each say the other third name is defensible, and Fredriksson accepts a two-name Autor-Hanson award as a fallback. They have not settled whether the two strands are one discovery or two. They also disagree on how much the 2023 and 2024 prizes overlap with the Katz strand. This position is not a single configuration: the Katz variant has three explicit supporters and the Dorn variant has two. The chair is one of the five and is counted as such.

Andersson and Friberg both prefer Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes for methods to estimate demand, market power and industry dynamics. They share the argument that the methods are widely used, have been tested over about thirty years, and have changed antitrust and applied practice. They also share the reservations that this is a method rather than a discovery about economic phenomena and that Bresnahan and Reiss (and Benkard and Levin) fall outside the cap. Friberg's citation explicitly adds dynamic models of industries, while Andersson's cites 'industry dynamics'. Friberg openly weighs the narrower breadth of support and his own IO proximity. Both list B001 and B037 as alternatives.

Strömberg and Teorell both prefer Persson, Tabellini and Besley for political economics on constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity. They share the view that the field is mature, field-creating, and a theory-plus-evidence programme. Both treat Besley's separable share as the weakest attribution point and regard a Persson-Tabellini pair as an acceptable fallback. Both read the 2024 institutions prize as asking a different question, but both acknowledge the Committee may see it as adjacent. Both accept that the cross-country constitutional evidence is less well identified than the theory. Neither is a member outside this agreement on the laureate set; Strömberg and Teorell also name B025 and B037 as alternatives.

Boppart alone prefers Obstfeld and Rogoff for the intertemporal open-economy framework and the exchange-rate disconnect puzzles. His case rests on a compact two-name attribution, durability and absorption into policy institutions. He concedes that the empirical puzzles remain unresolved and that the contribution is partly synthesis, so the citation should rest on the framework and not on a settled empirical result. Teorell, Hjalmarsson and Hassler question this point; Boppart calls B037 the most serious competitor if it is judged a single coherent contribution. B001 is listed as an alternative by Andersson, Friberg, Krusell, Fredriksson and Hassler, but that is not a preferred-configuration position.

Krusell alone prefers Kiyotaki and Moore for the collateral-constraint mechanism that amplifies and propagates fluctuations. His case rests on a clean two-name attribution, three decades of extension, and an asset-price channel he regards as distinct from the 2022 prize on banks. He acknowledges that direct empirical identification and the quantitative size of amplification are contested, and he argues against adding Gertler and Gilchrist. Boppart, Strömberg and Teorell list B025 as an alternative. Dreber explicitly declined to include it for lack of direct evidence on the collateral channel.

areas_of_agreement: All eleven round-1 files rest on the stated criteria of originality, breadth, durability and attribution. Several members explicitly say that opening support counts are not evidence of merit.
Autor and Hanson appear in all five B037 configurations, so the disagreement within B037 is confined to the third laureate and the breadth of the citation.

All six members whose preferred configuration is not B037 (Andersson, Boppart, Friberg, Krusell, Strömberg, Teorell) list B037 as an alternative. They describe its identification and policy reach as strong, and their stated reservations concern attribution and overlap.

Members across fields describe the two-name candidates B001 and B025 as having unusually clean attribution, and treat attribution cleanliness as a real advantage that is separate from scientific merit.

Members who discuss the China-shock evidence say the magnitude and persistence of the effects are debated, and several propose wording the citation around the evidence on adjustment, not settled welfare conclusions.
Members flag that the three-name cap forces exclusions in B022 (Bresnahan, Reiss), B037 (Dorn or Katz) and B045 (Besley), and none treats these exclusions as trivial.
scientific_disputes: B037: whether the skill-premium and task framework and the import-shock evidence form one discovery or two separable contributions (raised by Strömberg, Krusell, Boppart, Friberg, Andersson and the B037 supporters themselves).
B037: how large and persistent the China-shock effects are, and how robust shift-share designs and task measures are.
B022: whether structural estimation of demand and dynamic industries counts as a prize-worthy discovery or is mainly a method (Enflo, Andersson and Friberg all discuss this).

B001: whether a framework and synthesis with unresolved exchange-rate disconnect puzzles is as strong a basis as replicated empirical findings (Teorell, Hjalmarsson, Krusell and Hassler question this; Boppart defends the framework).

B025: whether the evidence for collateral-driven amplification is adequate when it rests largely on stylised and calibrated models (Dreber, Andersson, Boppart, Strömberg and Krusell himself raise this).

B045: how much the weaker causal identification of the cross-country constitutional evidence should count against a field whose strength is framework and testable predictions (Fredriksson, Teorell, Strömberg, Enflo and Hassler raise this).

B004, the chair's opening first choice and now a listed alternative: whether mixed empirical support for the protection-for-sale predictions weakens its case (Dreber, Friberg and the chair note this).
attribution_disputes: B037: Katz (Enflo, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson) versus Dorn (Dreber, Hassler, and Friberg's opening) as the third laureate. A two-name Autor-Hanson award is also on the table (Dreber's opening, and Fredriksson as a fallback).
B037: Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane are credited with the task framework but are not in the proposed laureate sets, which limits what the citation can claim for the framework.
B022: whether Bresnahan should displace Levinsohn, whether Reiss, Benkard and Levin should be recognised, and whether the BLP and Pakes dynamic strands can be credited together.
B045: whether Besley's state-capacity strand is separable enough for a trio, or whether Persson and Tabellini alone are cleaner.
B001: Boppart treats the Obstfeld-Rogoff pair as the consolidation of the framework, while Teorell points to credit owed to Sachs, Svensson and Lane.
B025: Krusell, Boppart and Strömberg want credit confined to Kiyotaki and Moore, with Gertler and Gilchrist excluded.
Helpman appears on both B004 and B008 (raised by Dreber and Enflo), so any trade configuration would have to credit him once.
maturity_disputes: B037: the China-shock papers date from the early 2010s and the long-run interpretation is still contested (Friberg). The B037 supporters argue that replication in other countries and refinement without reversal indicate adequate maturity.

B037, B045 and B025: members disagree on whether proximity to the 2023 (Goldin), 2024 (institutions and prosperity) and 2022 (banks and financial crises) prizes reduces the weight of an otherwise strong case, or whether the discoveries are distinct. Hjalmarsson, Enflo, Fredriksson, Teorell, Strömberg and Krusell each defend distinctness, while Strömberg, Fredriksson and the chair acknowledge the risk.

B001 and B022: the work is about thirty years old, and members do not raise a timing concern. Timing is not in dispute for B001, B022 and B045 and applies only to the B037 strands and to B025's modest empirical base.
B038 appears only as an alternative (Hjalmarsson) and is described by Dreber as better left to a later round because neighbourhood-effect findings have had less time for independent replication.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair: Hassler supports B037 with Dorn (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) in round 1, having moved from his opening first-ranked B004. Other members' responses (Dreber, Friberg, Boppart) quote the earlier B004 ranking. Hassler discloses co-authorship with Boppart, Friberg and Krusell (the secretary), and says he discounts his confidence in B045, B013 and B038 because they are near his own research. No tie to B037 candidates is stated.
Friberg discloses co-authorship with Hassler and Ellingsen (IJIO 2026), a spouse who is a former Swedish prime minister (stated as no apparent bearing), and IO proximity to B022.
Boppart discloses IIES collegiality and co-authorship with Krusell and Hassler, and a long collaboration with Klenow, a credited name on B031, which is not in his preferred configuration.
Krusell discloses co-authorship with Boppart and Hassler, macro-finance proximity to B025, and research on capital-skill complementarity adjacent to the B037 skill-premium strand.

Teorell discloses comparative-politics proximity to B045 and a shared Stockholm University affiliation with IIES colleagues. He also refers to a Stockholm connection that he attributes to Hassler's opening; no such flag appears in Hassler's round-1 file, so this is unspecified and may be clarified.
Hjalmarsson presented the 2023 prize (Goldin), which is adjacent to Katz's earlier collaboration, and states no personal or institutional tie to him.
Andersson discloses SSE affiliation alongside Dreber, Friberg and Strömberg, and Enflo discloses Lund collegial ties. Both are described as ties between members, not to candidates.

Fredriksson works in empirical labour economics, close to B037, and Dreber's metascience interest may increase the weight she gives to robustness. Both disclose no candidate tie. All flags are disclosed and not adjudicated.
questions_for_round2: B037: Is the committee prepared to treat the technology and task strand and the import-shock strand as a single discovery? If yes, can the Katz and Dorn variants each state in one sentence what that discovery is and why their third name is needed? If no, which strand should the citation honour, and should Autor and Hanson alone be considered?

B037 and Katz: Is the overlap between the skill-premium strand and the 2023 (Goldin) and 2024 prizes substantive or only thematic? Please name the incremental contribution that each of the three-laureate sets would add.

B022 against B001: What standard should apply to a method that changed practice (B022) compared with a framework with open puzzles (B001)? Are Andersson, Friberg and Boppart prepared to say what additional evidence would make their candidate rank above B037, and what would move them below it?

B025: Can any member cite direct empirical evidence for collateral-driven amplification beyond the post-2008 narrative, as Dreber asks? Does the committee regard the 2022 prize as covering this channel?

B045: Is Besley's state-capacity strand separable enough for a trio, or should Persson and Tabellini alone be considered? Could Strömberg and Teorell state why they regard B045 as distinct from the 2024 prize, and could Fredriksson or Enflo say what evidence would change their concern?

Teorell is asked to clarify the Stockholm connection he mentions and which candidate it concerns, and to confirm whether any member sees a conflict that should be disclosed beyond the notes already filed.

Members whose preferred configuration has two or fewer explicit supporters (Andersson, Boppart, Friberg, Krusell, Strömberg, Teorell) are asked which of the unresolved B037 attribution or scope points, if settled, would change their preferred configuration, and which would not.
summary.chair_observation: On explicit round-1 preferred configurations, B037 has five of eleven supporters, split three for Autor, Hanson and Katz and two for Autor, Dorn and Hanson. B022 and B045 each have two, and B001 and B025 one each. No single configuration reaches the six votes needed for a majority. These counts reflect stated round-1 positions only and are not inferences about final votes. The chair is among the B037 supporters and has tried to represent the minority positions on their own terms. The main open issues are whether B037 is one discovery or two, the Katz-versus-Dorn attribution, and how far adjacency to the 2022, 2023 and 2024 prizes should count. The substantive reservations about B022, B001, B025 and B045 concern method versus discovery, open puzzles, indirect empirical evidence and identification respectively. All assessments rest on members' own stated recollection of the literature, and the files do not independently verify sources.
